Slamhaus

Markdown in. C++ out. Ship something weird.

Slamhaus is a command-line static-site compiler for game developers, systems people, and anyone who would rather build a tiny tool than wrestle a frontend stack. Write ordinary Markdown, add typed UI when you need interaction, and embed C++ that compiles to WebAssembly.

Getting started · View examples · Open the live showcase · API cheatsheet

No package maze. No hydration tax. No handwritten JavaScript for supported interaction. Just a compiler, a project folder, and a dist/ directory you can put anywhere.

Why Slamhaus?

Built like a game-engine subsystem

The compiler is modular C++17: parsing, validation, routing, rendering, the language server, and the WebAssembly bridge are explicit systems. It is fast to run, straightforward to inspect, and comfortable to extend.

Markdown stays the source of truth

Portable .md remains portable GFM. .slam adds only the things a site needs: metadata, typed UI, and optional C++ behavior. Your content is still readable in a text editor, a diff, or a terminal.

Interactive without the frontend ceremony

Name a component, bind an event, write a typed function, and let Slamhaus generate the DOM IDs, module manifest, argument conversion, and accessible output. The browser gets the runtime; you get to think in C++.

Static by default, capable when needed

Landing pages, docs, portfolios, release notes, and blogs emit plain HTML and CSS. Add Emscripten only to the pages that actually need it: calculators, tools, toys, canvas experiments, and game-like interfaces.

Deterministic and deployable

Routes, links, partials, assets, metadata, and accessibility checks happen at build time. The result is a complete site in dist/, ready for GitHub Pages, an object bucket, a CDN, or a USB stick.

A small language

Pages use .md when they should remain portable and .slam when they need Slam UI or executable code. Site configuration lives in slamhaus.yaml.

Ready
S L A M // *

The complete working version is on the live showcase.

Start a project 

slamhaus init my-site
cd my-site
slamhaus check --strict
slamhaus build
slamhaus serve

The short version 

content       -> Markdown and Slam UI you can read
compiler      -> routes, HTML, CSS, diagnostics, and modules
typed C++     -> optional WebAssembly behavior
dist/         -> a boring, portable website you can ship

Slamhaus is a good fit when you want:

  • a personal site or studio landing page without a JavaScript framework;
  • documentation that stays close to source control and the command line;
  • game-dev-flavoured UI and browser toys written in familiar C++;
  • a small, inspectable compiler instead of a cloud build service;
  • accessible semantic HTML with responsive controls from the start;
  • a static deployment story that remains cheap, cacheable, and portable.

It is deliberately not a full game engine, CMS, SPA framework, or proprietary renderer. Bring your own rendering technology when you need one; Slamhaus handles the site, the document, and the bridge to the browser.
